/behandelingen/angst-tandartsangst/.title: Fear of the dentist? Oral care practice Veenendaal helps

/behandelingen/angst-tandartsangst/.text:
Treatment for patients with dental anxiety

Many people experience dental anxiety, and that's not weird at all. It can make access to dental care more difficult and can lead to delay behaviour, which will ultimately cause more problems. In our practice we understand this fear and do everything we can to make you as comfortable as possible. With our calm approach and gentle treatment we help you to overcome your fear and receive care without stress.

HOW ARE WE GOING TO FEAR?

Our approach is always calm, friendly and patient. We understand that every person is different and that the dental experience can sometimes be overwhelming. That's why we take the time to listen to your concerns and guide you through every step of the treatment.

Soft communication: We explain every step of the treatment and make sure you always know what's happening.

Atmospheric environment: Our practice is designed for comfort and tranquility, so you feel comfortable. From decoration to lighting, everything is focused on a relaxed atmosphere.

Choice of treatment methods: We offer different treatment options, such as local anaesthetics and soothing techniques, so you always choose what works best for you.

Quiet and pain-free approach

Our treatments are designed to minimize pain and reassure you. For patients with dental anxiety we have developed special techniques that ensure a pain-free experience.

Painless treatments: Thanks to modern equipment and techniques, we can perform most treatments without pain. You'll find the treatments are less intense than you might expect.

Slow and careful approach: We take time for every treatment and work at your pace. You can always ask for a break if you want to relax.

Tips to relax to the dentist

For many people the thought of the dentist may be a source of fear, but there are ways to reduce this fear. Here are some tips that can help you relax to go to the dentist:

Respiratory exercises: Breathe deeply and out before your appointment to calm your nerves. This will help you stay calm and let go of the tension.

Bring a friend or family member: It may be reassuring to bring someone you trust to your appointment. They can support you and help you feel at ease.

Plan your appointment at a quiet time: Choose a time for your appointment when you are not in a hurry or stressed by other obligations. This ensures a more relaxed experience.

Use relaxation techniques: Listen to calming music or use a relaxing app to distract your thoughts during treatment.

Communicate your fears: Tell the dentist or assistant about your fears. We adapt the treatment to your needs and make you feel comfortable.

Our fear-free dentist in Veenendaal offers a comfortable dental experience.

FAQ
Is it possible to be treated under mild sedation?

Yes, we offer mild sedation for patients who feel extra anxious. This ensures that you undergo treatment in a relaxed state, without being unconscious.

Should I discuss my fear with the dentist?

/behandelingen/white-spots-verwijderen-w.title: Remove white spots at dentist Oral care practice Veenendaal

/behandelingen/white-spots-verwijderen-w.text:
Remove white spots without drilling

Having white spots on your teeth can make for a less radiant smile. Fortunately, the removal of these stains is now possible without the need to drill. In our practice, we offer effective treatment to remove white spots in a safe and painless way. With the right care and treatment, we can help you get another radiant smile without discomfort.

CAUSES OF WHITE VICTIMS ON TANDS

White spots can have different causes. They are usually caused by an accumulation of dental plaque, poor oral hygiene, or due to the excessive use of fluoride in youth. They can also be caused by too much acid in the mouth, for example by certain foods or beverages. Other causes may be related to the structural structure of the teeth, such as early tooth decay or demineralisation of the tooth enamel.

It is important to know that white spots are not holes, but an indication of incomplete mineralization of the glaze. If they're not treated, they can eventually lead to cavities. That is why it is important to deal with them in good time.

ICON treatment: How does it work?

The ICON treatment is a modern technique specially developed for removing white spots without drilling. It is a simple and painless treatment where a special liquid is applied to the white spots. This liquid penetrates the pores of the teeth and fills the demineralization, causing the spots to disappear.

The treatment starts with a thorough cleansing of your teeth. The ICON gel is then applied to the white spots. The gel is activated by a special light, which corrects the demineralisation process and reduces white spots. This treatment is fast, effective and completely painless.

Result and safety

The result of the ICON treatment is often immediately visible, and the white spots are significantly reduced or completely eliminated. Because the treatment does not require drilling, it is a soft and safe way to repair your teeth without damaging the tooth enamel.

The ICON treatment is safe and approved by dental professionals. It is an effective solution for reducing aesthetic stains on your teeth without using invasive techniques. After the treatment you can smile again with confidence, without worrying about the white spots.

To remove white spots on your teeth, visit our practice in Veenendaal.

FAQ
Is the ICON treatment painful?

No, the ICON treatment is completely painless. You will not experience any discomfort during treatment.

/behandelingen/pijnloze-gebitsreiniging-.title: Pain-free dental cleaning (GBT)
/behandelingen/pijnloze-gebitsreiniging-.metaDescription: Enjoy a painless dental cleansing! Dentist Oral Care Practice Veenendaal offers GBT treatments for a healthy and fresh mouth.
/behandelingen/pijnloze-gebitsreiniging-.text:
Painless dental cleaning with GBT

A healthy mouth starts with a good cleaning, and that is exactly what we offer with our painless dental cleaning via Guided Biofilm Therapy (GBT). This modern and advanced technique ensures that your teeth and gums are thoroughly cleaned without experiencing any discomfort. Thanks to GBT, we can efficiently remove plaque and tartar, while reducing the risk of gum problems such as gingivitis and parodontitis.

WHAT IS GUIDED BIOFILM THERAPY?

Guided Biofilm Therapy (GBT) is a revolutionary method for dental cleaning using biofilm detection and removal. Biofilm is a thin layer of bacteria that forms on your teeth and gums and can cause plaque and tartar. GBT uses a special device to make this biofilm visible, so that we can remove it aimlessly without damaging your teeth or gums.

The treatment is extremely effective and painless. It ensures a thorough cleaning of your mouth, removing tartar, plaque and other undesirable substances. GBT makes it possible to clean hard-to-reach areas in your mouth, which contributes to optimal oral health.

Advantages of GBT

GBT offers various benefits, both for you as a patient, and for your oral health:

Painless and comfortable: Because the technique is extremely careful, you will not experience any pain during treatment.

Thorough cleaning: GBT provides deep cleansing of your teeth and gums, which helps prevent gum infections and cavities.

Healthier gums: By effectively removing biofilm, GBT helps keep your gums healthy and prevent inflammation.

Improved oral health: Regular treatments with GBT can safely and efficiently remove plaque and tartar, which contributes to a long-lasting healthy mouth.

Less sensitivity: Because the treatment is so mild, the chance of sensitivity or irritation of your gums is minimal.

Does Guided Biofilm Therapy hurt?

No, GBT is known for its soft approach. We use a fine powder-air jet instead of sharp instruments, so the treatment is also suitable for people with sensitive teeth or gum fears.

How long does a GBT treatment take?
Can I just eat after the treatment?
Who is this treatment suitable for?

GBT is suitable for almost anyone who wants to improve their oral health and prevent gum problems. Whether you have healthy gums or have mild gum infections, this treatment can help keep your mouth perfectly clean and healthy.

Specific situations where GBT can be particularly useful:

Gingival problems: If you suffer from inflamed gums (gingivitis) or parodontitis, GBT can help to reduce inflammation and restore your gums.

Prevention of cavities: By removing biofilm, you can significantly reduce the risk of punctures and other dental problems.

People with sensitive teeth: GBT is a gentle and comfortable way of cleaning, so it is an excellent option for people with sensitive gums or teeth.

Experience painless dental cleansing at our dental practice in Veenendaal.



FAQ
Is GBT really painless?

Yes, GBT is an extremely painless treatment. You will experience no discomfort, and it is far less invasive than traditional cleaning methods.

/behandelingen/tandvleesbehandeling-paro.title: Gingival treatment (Parodontitis)
/behandelingen/tandvleesbehandeling-paro.metaDescription: Any gum problems? Dentist Oral Care Practice Veenendaal offers effective treatments for parodontitis in a quiet and caring environment.
/behandelingen/tandvleesbehandeling-paro.text:
Treatment of inflamed gums and parodontitis

Gingivitis and parodontitis are common gum problems that can seriously affect your oral health if they are not treated in time. Fortunately, these conditions can often be treated well with proper care and prevention. In our practice we offer expert treatments to remedy inflamed gums and parodontitis and restore the health of your gums. We're doing this in a caring, quiet, professional way, so you can feel comfortable.

SYMPTOMS OF MILK DISCLOSURE

Recognizing the symptoms of gum inflammation is important to avoid further complications. Common symptoms include:

Bleeding gums: The gums may bleed, especially when brushing or using floss.

Red, swollen gums: Your gums may be swollen, tender and red, suggesting inflammation.

Retreating gums: Parodontitis can cause gums to withdraw, making the teeth look longer.

Bad breath: A persistent bad breath may also indicate gum inflammation or infection.

Pain or discomfort: Sometimes gums can be painful, especially if it's inflamed.

If you experience any of these symptoms, it is important to make an appointment quickly with the dentist or dental hygienist. Early treatment prevents inflammation from getting worse and spreading to the underlying tissues.

Professional cleaning & deep cleaning

Treatment of gum inflammation and parodontitis usually starts with professional cleansing. This process consists of removing plaque and tartar, which can accumulate under the gum edge and cause inflammation. This is done by a dental hygienist or dentist, who ensures that your teeth and gums are thoroughly cleaned.

In more advanced cases of parodontitis deep cleansing may be necessary. This means that we also clean under the gums to remove deeply rooted tartar and bacteria. The goal is to fight the infection, reduce inflammation and make your gums healthy.

In some cases, additional treatments can also be carried out, such as cleaning the root surfaces of the teeth or using antibiotics to fight bacteria.

Causes and prevention

The main causes of gum inflammation and parodontitis are poor oral hygiene, smoking, poor diet and certain medical conditions. Dental plaque, a sticky film of bacteria, is the main cause of these diseases. If dental plaque is not regularly removed by brushing and flossing properly, it can harden to tartar, which is the cause of gum problems.

How can you prevent gum infection?

Brush twice a day: Brush your teeth thoroughly, at least twice a day, with a fluoride toothpaste.

Floss daily: Flossing helps to remove plaque between your teeth and along the gum edge.

Healthy nutrition: A balanced diet, rich in vitamins and minerals, supports healthy gums.

Avoid smoking: Smoking increases the risk of gum inflammation and parodontitis, so smoking cessation is crucial for healthy teeth.

Regular checks: Visit the dentist or dental hygienist regularly for professional cleaning and checks.

By incorporating these simple habits into your daily routine, you can avoid many gum problems and maintain your long-term oral health.

Our dental practice in Veenendaal offers treatments for gum problems.

FAQ
How do I know if I have gum infection?

The symptoms of gum inflammation include bleeding gums, swollen or red spots, and bad breath. If you have these symptoms, it's important to make an appointment with the dentist.

/behandelingen/preventie-mondhygienist/.text:
Professional dental cleaning and prevention

Healthy teeth begin with good prevention. In our practice, we represent the importance of regular checks and good oral hygiene. Our dental hygienists not only help you keep your teeth clean, but also provide valuable advice to prevent dental problems. Together we work on maintaining healthy, radiant teeth, so that you always feel comfortable laughing, talking and eating.

WHAT DOES A MONDHYGIENIST DO?

A dental hygienist is a specialist in oral health. She not only helps you remove plaque and tartar, but also gives you personal advice on how to improve your oral hygiene. This can be done by giving cleaning instructions, advising on toothpastes and mouthwashing, and discussing your eating and drinking habits.

In addition, the dental hygienist treats gum problems, such as gingivitis, and can advise you on the right technique for flossing and using other tools, such as ragers or toothpicks. Also when treating more advanced gum problems the dental hygienist can help by performing deeper cleansing of the gums.

Prevention of piercing & gum inflammation

Preventing cavities and gum infection is an essential part of oral health. Regular brushing and removal of dental plaque is very important.

Cabins: Cavities are formed by bacteria that accumulate in plaque and affect the teeth.

Gingivitis: This often starts with irritated gums that bleeds while brushing.

PITCH AND CLEANING OPINION

Brush twice a day, floss daily, use good mouthwash, avoid sugar and sours, visit the dental hygienist regularly.

It is recommended to go to the dental hygienist twice a year for professional cleaning and monitoring.

What are faces?

Facings are thin shields placed on the front of your teeth to give them an aesthetic improvement, used in discoloured, damaged or crooked teeth.

MATERIAL: US COMPOSITE. PORSELEIN

Composite faces: cheaper, one appointment, slightly less sustainable.
Porcelain faces: stronger, more sustainable, laboratory work, more natural result.

How's the treatment going?

Two agreements: first assessment and preparation (sharpening, printing), then placing the final facings.

RESULTS AND SUSTAINABILITY

Composite: 5-7 years. Porcelain: 10+ years.

What are algorithms and how do they work?

Aligners, also called transparent brackets, are custom-made, transparent trays that gradually shift your teeth to the desired position. Almost invisible, easy to remove during eating, drinking and brushing teeth.

You wear each set 20 to 22 hours a day, usually two weeks, after which a new set follows.

ADVANTAGE

Aesthetically attractive, removable, more comfortable than metal brackets, fewer dental visits needed.

Treatment duration and costs

Usually between 6 and 18 months, depending on the correction. Costs vary with severity and duration.

For whom?

Mild to moderate abnormalities: crooked teeth, overbite/underbite, holes between teeth. With more complex jaw problems, traditional braces can be better.

FAQ
Are aligners really invisible?

/behandelingen/tanden-trekken-extracties.title: Teeth pulling (extractions)
/behandelingen/tanden-trekken-extracties.text:
When is an extraction required?

Pulling a tooth is sometimes necessary to restore your oral health: severe damage due to tooth decay, fractures, infections, crooked tooth or overpopulation of the tooth. Also for gum problems or wisdom teeth that cause problems.

SPECIES OF EXTRACTION: SIMPLE & CHIRUGIC

Simple extraction: visible, easily accessible tooth, with pliers pulled under local anaesthetic.

Surgical extraction: tooth deep under gums or broken, sometimes split into pieces, possibly mild anesthesia.

How's the treatment going?

Call, local anaesthetic, extraction (max ~30 min), after care instructions. Sutures removed after a few weeks if necessary.

RECOVERY, SWILLING AND NAZORG

Mild swelling normal, first 24 hours no hard/hot food, cold compress helps, mouthwashing with hot salt water, control arrangements for surgical extractions.

FAQ
Is pulling a tooth painful?

Not with local anaesthetic; but pressure/movement palpable, no pain.

Different types of prostheses

Full dentures: replaces all teeth in upper or lower jaw.
Partial prosthesis: fills empty spaces, attached with clammers to your own teeth.
Implant-based prosthesis: fixed on dental implants for extra stability.

WHEN YOU NEED A PROTHESIS?

In case of loss of multiple teeth or irreparable damage, due to old age, tooth decay or accident.

How does it measure?

Examination, jaw print, preliminary prosthesis to adapt and adapt, final prosthesis after a few weeks (laborative work).

Tips for maintenance

Clean daily with soft brush and prosthetic cleaner (no ordinary toothpaste), out at night in water/solution, regularly check for cracks, avoid hard food, annual check-date.

FAQ
How long does dentures last?

5 to 10 years depending on maintenance.

In case of damage due to deep hole, fracture or wear (crown), or to replace a missing tooth (bridge).

Ceramics: Aesthetic, natural colour, suitable for front teeth.
Porcelain: strong, durable, good colour match.
Zirconium: very strong, suitable for choice, aesthetic.

How's the treatment going?

Preparing tooth (sharpening), printing, possibly temporary crown, final crown/bridge places manufactured in laboratory.

Duration and maintenance

5 to 15 years depending on material and oral hygiene. Good brush and floss routine extends life.

Recovery and aftercare

Inflamed or infected nerve caused by deep hole, damage or spread infection. Save the tooth and relieve the pain.

HOW DOES THE TREATMENT WORK?

Anesthesia, small hole to the nerve, remove infected tissue, clean/disinfect canal and fill, possibly close with a crown. Mostly 1-2 sessions.

_

Sustained toothache, pain in biting, prolonged sensitivity to cold/warm, swelling gums, discoloration of the tooth.

RECOVERY AND NAZORG

Temporary sensitivity normal, soft eating recommended, hard/sticky diet avoid.

FAQ
Is root canal treatment painful?

Pretty painless with good anesthesia.

How long does a root canal take?

60-90 minutes, sometimes a second appointment for filling / crown.

What should I do after treatment?

Soft food, treated tooth not directly burden, possibly painkillers.

Oral care & Mouth hygiene . . . Prevention as a basis for a healthy mouth

Cristian Zandi June 19, 2026

Intro: Denial of brushing in children is rarely stubbornness. Poor oral hygiene at a young age has real consequences: holes in baby teeth, damage to permanent selection, effect on self-confidence.

Sections: Why does a child refuse to brush teeth (control/autonomy at <3 years of age; taste/feeling/sensory sensitivity in older children)  caries can damage permanent tooth underneath) . . Frequently made parents' mistakes (physical compulsion, threatening with the dentist, no fixed routine, using toothpaste for adults) . . Practical tips (1. Make it a game, 2. Give choice within limits, 3. Prefer yourself, 4. let child first try, 5. real compliments instead of candy, 6. for sensory sensitivity: soft hair, first without toothpaste) From what age do self-cleaning (most children up to 7-8 years do not yet have enough fine motor skills; rule of thumb: can the child tie shoes himself) What the pediatrician can mean (Just Cool method; first visit around 2nd birthday, no treatment, only introduction) . . Practical guide toothbrush/toothpaste (fluoride dosage: up to 2yr rice grain without fluoride, 2-6yr pea size 1000ppm, from 6yr strip 1cm 1450ppm; twice daily, evening polishing most important) When using professional help (persistent resistance, sensory processing disorder, discoloration/stains/bad breath/tick pain = fast to dentist).

(less saliva during sleep = more risk) Is an electric toothbrush better for children? (often, unless child doesn't like the vibrations) • Can I use mouthwash for my child? (recommended under 6 years) My child is afraid of the dentist, what can I do? ('tell-show-do' approach) Why are baby teeth so important? (keep space for permanent teeth).

UNCATEGORIZED
Invisalign during pregnancy: What you need to know
Cristian Zandi May 17, 2026

Intro: Invisalign is non-invasive, usually safe during pregnancy provided oral health is stable and accompanied by dentist/ortodontist. Pregnancy involves more sensitive gums, increased risk of gum inflammation, nausea/ vomiting.

Sections: Is Invisalign safe during pregnancy (always discuss with treatment, never start/pause/change on your own initiative) • Materials and digital scans (SmartTrack thermoplastic, BPA free; iTero 3D scan is not X-ray) • Effects of pregnancy hormones (pregnancy gingivitis: more sensitive gums, faster bleeding/swelling; extra important for Invisalign because it takes many hours of teeth for aligners) . Morning sickness, vomiting and wearing (20-22 hours/day; after vomiting: Rinse with water/fluoride mouthwash, clean aligners, wait 30 min with brushing ivm weakened glaze by stomach acid) inform treatment, often continue if no complications; to start: second trimester often more practical, less nausea; third trimester: long lag back less comfortable).

Practical tips: 2x/day brush with fluoride toothpaste, clean daily between teeth, do not return after eating/drinking without rinsing, only drink water with aligners in, clean aligners daily according to instructions.

FAQ: Can I have X-rays taken during pregnancy? (not automatically prohibited, preferably delayed unless urgently needed)  . . Does my baby need calcium from my teeth? (no, misunderstanding of calcium from food/body stock) What if I'm wearing algorithms less than 20-22 hours? (treatment delays, contact treatment) Can I have attachments placed during pregnancy? (usually, depending on comfort/nausea) . . Should I stop with bleeding gums? (not on your own initiative, contact; keep brushing carefully).

Medical note: information is general, does not replace any personal medical advice, always discuss with dentist, orthodontist, obstetrician or gynecologist.

Transparent cost comparison (aligners higher start-up costs due to 3D scans/labwork, but lock bar more consultations over time . . . total costs often comparable) . . Predictability thanks to 3D technology (ClinCheck digital simulation shows final result) . . . Patient testimonials (reference to RealSelf.com independent data about Invisalign and Braces).

(removable = easier oral hygiene in pregnancy-sensitive gums; refers to the separate Invisalign pregnancy article).

Parodontitis vs. Denture: Scientific criteria for the right treatment choice
Cristian Zandi April 19, 2026

Intro: at pockets deeper than 9mm impossible for patient to effectively remove bacteria chronic inflammatory source with systemic consequences (heart and vascular disease, impaired blood sugar in diabetes).

Conservation of natural teeth: medical preference if >50% bone support. Treatment pathway: scaling/root planning, in advanced cases flap surgery. Advantages: preserve natural chewing power and proprioception, jaw bone remains stimulated. Cons: requires iron discipline in oral hygiene, risk of recurrence. Costs: lower in the short term than full prosthesis, but may be incurred by years of aftercare.

The transition to dentures: Immediate prosthesis (pass shape rarely optimally due to bone absorption, first months adjustments/rebasing required) . . . Click teeth on implants (more stability, less discomfort in speech/eating) . . Psychological/social impact (acceptation is mental transition, getting used to change in speech/eating).

Examples of practice: references to external case-study sources are now anonymised/de-linked in this export (see note above) . . . . . . . . Also, "When things go wrong: Complex interventions do not always have a favourable outcome, which underlines the importance of a fair medical indication and realistic expectations. '

FAQ: Is dentures a definitive solution for pain? (often, new challenge is getting used to strange object) . (parodontitis treatment usually requires additional insurance; complete dentures 75% covered by basic insurance, clinkebit implants not always complete) (no, learn to chew again, lower bite power at first).

Conclusion: parodontitis treatment focuses on conservation of natural function, dentures resolve chronic pain/infection. Link to prosthesis / dentures page.

Cristian Zandi April 15, 2026

Step plan daily cleaning: 1) rinse after each meal under lukewarm running water, 2) thoroughly brush 1-2x/day with special prosthetic brush (outside and inside), top sink with water/towel against fracture, 3) clean own oral cavity (tooth, palate, tongue with soft brush).

Porcelain or composite facings: What is the best choice for your teeth?
Cristian Zandi April 12, 2026

What are facings: thin shields on front of teeth .

Main differences: Material (porcelain=ceramic, composite=tooth-coloured synthetic resin). Durability (porcelain 10-15+ year, wear-resistant). Aesthetics (porcelain retains shine, colourfast, light falls through it more naturally). Treatment (porcelain requires more preparation / grinding, composite often direct/non-prep). Repair (composed easy to repair in the seat, porcelain at break usually complete replacement).

When porcelain: larger stand defects, strong discolorations, durable color-resistant high quality solution. When composite: subtle corrections, small cracks (diastemen), broken edges, faster/cost-efficient.

Costs: NZa-fixed rates + variable technical costs (lab costs); porcelain more expensive by laboratory work.

Preventive Mouth Care: Scientific Underbuilt Methods for Maintaining Your Mouth Health
Cristian Zandi April 10, 2026

5 pillars: 1) Mechanical Plaque removal (2x/day, 2 full minutes, focus on gum-tooth transition/sulcus). 2) Interdental Cleaning (toothbrush cleans only ~60% of the surface; daily ragers/picks/floss wire required). 3) Fluoride and Remineralization (fluoride binds to glaze, stimulates remineralization, protects against acid). 4) Nutrition habits and Acid-Base Balance (frequency more important than sugar; max 7 eating/drinking moments per day including 3 main meals, gives saliva time to neutralize). 5) Professional Prevention and Diagnostics (periodic research detects problems early; professional cleaning removes tartar that cannot be brushed away at home).

FAQ: How often do you change your toothbrush? (every 3 months, earlier in the case of raspberry hair) (completion, no replacement; especially in specific conditions on advice) Is electric more effective than manual? (yes, clinically proven in oscillating-rotating types . . . significantly more adhesive removal and less gum inflammation).

Why is professional dental cleaning essential?
Cristian Zandi February 15, 2026

The need for prevention: Unreachable spots when brushing → plaque calcified to tartar → gum irritation (redness/bleeds) → untreated inflammation can spread to jaw bone.

Direct benefits: prevention of damage (less risk of piercing/toothing problems), freshness (less breath odour of bacteria in tartar), natural appearance (surface discoloration due to food/smoking disappear).

FAQ: Is dental cleansing painful? (usually not, can be sensitive to lightly inflamed gums, intensity adjustable) Why clean without complaints? (tooth meat disorders often do not cause pain in the early stages, waiting for pain = often too late)

Scientific accountability: ADA evidence-based directive based on 72 studies . . . professional cleaning (scaling and root planning) is the standard non-surgical treatment for parodontitis, improves detectable gum health and helps prevent tooth loss. /ontstoken-tandvlees-symptomen-behandeli.text:
MONDESONITY
Inflamed gums: Research on symptoms and treatment solutions
Cristian Zandi January 27, 2026

How do you recognize unhealthy gums: Healthy gums are pink, lying tight, not bleeding. Signals: bleeding when brushing/flossing/hard food, dark red/swollen/glossy color, bad breath (halitosis).

From Gingivitis to Parodontitis: gingivitis = superficial inflammation by plaque; untreated extends to jaw bone = parodontitis with 'pockets' full of bacteria, can lead to irreversible bone loss.

Main causes: dental plaque/biofilm (primary), hardened to tartar; risk factors: smoking/tobacco, systemic diseases (diabetes), hormonal fluctuations.

When professional help: you cannot remove tartar and bacteria deep in pockets; mouth hygienist measures DPSI score and thoroughly cleans pockets.

FAQ: Does gum treatment hurt? (No, anesthetic if necessary in the case of deeper cleanings) (often partly through supplementary insurance, T-series codes).

Sources: 3 scientific articles quoted (Journal of Clinical Periodicology 2018, Nature Reviews Disease Primers 2017, BMC Oral Health 2006) .

ALIGNER
Choosing to pull braces: Why, the costs and experiences
Cristian Zandi January 7, 2026

Why draw tooth: Lack of space for teeth too big for the jaw; strategic pulling creates space to tidy up other teeth, prevents relapse (relapse).

Is it a sin? A teeth that are too tight is more difficult to keep clean = more likely to cause piercing/tooth inflammation; This is an investment in long-term health.

Choose which: 4 (most common, premolars, symmetrical above/below), 2 (top jaw only, e.g. overbite), baby teeth in children (to steer breakthrough of permanent tooth).

Treatment: anesthesia → extraction → recovery (next orthodontist appointment after 1-2 weeks).

In adults: jaw fully grown, attract more often only option (v. children where jaw can sometimes be widened).

Costs 2026: NZa codes H10 (tractions, excluding anaesthetic), H15 (difficult extraction). Children up to 18 often reimbursed through basic insurance as part of orthodontic indication; adults need additional insurance.

FAQ: Do holes/cavities remain visible? (No, orthodontist uses space to shift teeth, crevices close completely) Is it painful? Are there any alternatives? ('strips'/sharpened sides, or jaw broadening' examined by X-rays).

/hoe-werken-doorzichtige-aligners/.text:
ALIGNER
How do transparent algorithms work?
Cristian Zandi December 28, 2025

What are algorithms: custom-made transparent plastic cases (Invisalign, Spark), smooth medical material, removable, no irritation like metal brackets.

Scientific action bone remodeling (bone remodeling): aligner exerts slight constant pressure via tooth root on parodontal ligament and jaw bone. Pressure side activates osteoclasts (break down old bone), tension side stimulates osteoblasts (create new bone). Tooth shifts ~0,2-0.3mm per algorithm. Sometimes dental attachments for extra grip. Research shows similar effectiveness as traditional brackets consistently wear.

Treatment process: 1) Diagnosis and planning . Digital 3D scan, software plan with predefined end result. 2) Production of tailor made aligners, each set for 1-2 weeks. 3) Carrying and changing 20-22 hours/day, checking every 6-8 weeks (less frequent than fixed bracket).

Aftercare and retention: fixed or removable retainer needed to maintain result for life.

Sources: 2 scientific articles quoted (Angle Orthodontist 2015 "systematic review efficiacy clear algorithms"; Journal of Orthodontic Science 2023 и Clear Aligner Therapy Review) (see live page for PubMed links).

/wanneer-vullingen-vervangen/.text:
COMPLETIONS
When to replace fillings? This is how you know the right moment
Cristian Zandi December 24, 2025

Replacers: damaged/broken fillings (breaks allow bacteria in), pain or tenderness (may indicate leaky/sorted filling), discoloration around the filling (sign of secondary caries), loose-sitting/inoperative fillings (fast replacement to prevent further damage).

Life time per material: composite 5-10 years, amalgam 10-15 years, ceramic 15+ years. Regular monitoring is important.

Why eventually replace: limited life of filling material (wear from chewing forces), fracture/damage due to trauma (hard bite, teeth grinding), changes due to aging, caries in adjacent tooth, retreating gums (shuffle edge of filling).

Effects of non-replacement: worsening tooth decay (bacteria penetrate leaking filling = secondary caries, often unnoticed), inflammation/infection of the teeth nerve (severe pain/swelling), greater chance of root canal treatment or crown.

FAQ: How do you know to replace a filling? (klinical examination + X-rays if any) (no, only in case of problems such as pain/leakage/caries) . (yes, micro-leakage due to thermal changes/expansion/shrink .JADA study confirms some leakage even with new fillings) Is replacing painful? (usually not, with local anaesthetic).

/alles-wat-je-moet-weten-over-het-vullen.text:
COMPLETIONS
What instruments does the dentist use when filling a hole?
Cristian Zandi December 21, 2025

5 steps: 1) Diagnosis and preparation (anesthetic on gums/tooth). 2) Cleaning the tooth / removing damaged tissue (touched tissue removed without damaging healthy tooth tissue). 3) Filling the hole (placed suitable filling). 4) Shape and adjust (composed harden out under special light). 5) Control and aftercare (bite-on-paper test to check discomfort in chewing).

Types of fillings: Composite (likes tooth glaze, for front teeth, aesthetic, customizable tooth shape). Porcelain (for severely damaged teeth or aesthetic desire, stronger than composite, less discoloration, ideal for visible teeth). Amalgam (mixture silver/tin/copper/sink, durable and cheap, for choice, not aesthetically textured dark in color).

Costs: vary €50-€200 depending on type of filling, size hole, practice; amalgam cheaper than composite/porcelain.

Aftercare: first days no hard/sticky food, careful with treated tooth, regular brushing and flossing.

FAQ: Does it hurt? (no due to anesthesia, mild sensitivity after normal) (20 min to 1 hour, depending on size/type) (for wear/damage/release).

/hoe-vaak-tanden-bleken/.text:
_
How many teeth whitening? Guide to safe and lasting results
Cristian Zandi October 31, 2025

Intro: professional refresher treatment recommended every 6-12 months; frequency depends on daily habits (coffee/tea/red wine/smoking), type of treatment, oral hygiene/diet, dental health.

Why discolour teeth: extrinsic discoloration (surface, easy to remove with whitening toothpaste) vs. intrinsic discoloration (deep in dental bone, professional treatment required). Causes: coffee/tea/fresh drinks/red wine, food colours, smoking, ageing (thinner glaze).

How does bleaching work: hydrogen peroxide or carbamide peroxide breaks down color pigments through oxidation reaction. Professional up to 6% peroxide (safe under supervision) vs. freely available max 0.1%.

Methods: Home pales (to size bleaches + gel, few hours/day over weeks, own pace) vs. In-practice bleaching (stronger gels + light, faster result, accurate guidance).

Frequency: professional refreshment every 6-12 months or 1-2x/year; home products less sustainable result, professional guidance recommended.

Duration result: on average 1-2 years, with good care up to 3 years. Tips: 2x brushing, floss thread/ragers, 2x/year dental hygienist, smoking cessation, reducing colorful nutrition. Result: 5-10 shades improvement average.

Conditions: from 18 years of age, not in pregnancy/feeding, first treat cavities, crowns/facings/fills remain unchanged in colour (may consider replacement after bleaching.

Direct aftercare "white diet" first 48 hours: recommended milk/yoghurt/white cheese/white meat/white rice/paste with white sauce; avoid coffee/tea/red wine/colored sauces/red beet. Sensitivity: light and temporary, toothpaste for sensitive teeth helps.

Costs: professional home-bleaching with custom spoon €235-€295 (spoon reusable, refresh cheaper); cosmetic treatment, not reimbursed by health insurance.

FAQ: How many times a year? (max 1-2x professional) How long does the result last? (1-3 years) . . Is self bleaching safe? (freely available products bring risks, professional guidance is safest).

/vanaf-welke-leeftijd-tanden-bleken/.metaDescription: Read from what age teeth whitening is safe and discover tips for a radiant smile, risks and costs.
/vanaf-welke-leeftijd-tanden-bleken/.text:
_
Teeth bleaching: From what age and important tips
Cristian Zandi October 31, 2025

Key issues: legally authorised from 18 years; max 1 treatment/year recommended; professional bleaching prevents glaze damage; average cost ~€300, sometimes reimbursed through supplementary insurance.

From what age: dental/specialist under 18 years of age were not legally permitted, even with parental consent.

Why 18-year limit: Teeth in development, nerve chamber (pulpa) relatively high = higher risk of damage; only safe in adult teeth.

Minors: Some home bleaching products claim safely from 12 years of age, but dentists strongly advise against this risk of permanent glaze damage.

Frequency: max 1x per year; too frequent bleaching can lead to porous glaze and lasting sensitivity.

Risks: irritation gums, hypersensitivity to cold/warm drinks, especially to cheap home sets.

Costs: in-office from €200/session, home pale with measuring spoons from €250, average ~€300 complete journey; cosmetic surgery, usually not reimbursed by basic insurance.

Tips for whitening teeth without whitening: mild whitening toothpaste 2x/day, daily (water) flosser (safe from 12 years), coloring food limit, tongue cleaning daily.

FAQ: What age do you get to bleach? (at least 18 years) How old for faces? (also mostly from 18, when jaw has fully grown) How many times a year? Is it reimbursed? (depends on supplementary policy, basic insurance does not usually cover).

_
Your Teeth Bleached: The Risks and How You Avoid them
Cristian Zandi October 31, 2025

Peroxide risks and legal limits: High concentrated hydrogen peroxide can affect tooth roots. EU rules: dentists/mond hygienists max 6% peroxide per treatment; beauty specialists max 0.1%; retail products max 0.1%. Using chlorin at home is strongly not recommended.

Structural damage: bleaching makes glaze/toothbone more porous = more sensitive to new discoloration; incorrect/excessive application can lead to damaged glaze, sensitivity, more carie risk.

Sensitivity and irritation: temporary sensitivity to heat/cold/sweet/acid; gum irritation in case of improper application/poor fitting spoon, in rare cases gum burns.

Professional vs. self bleaching: professionally = correct concentration, protected gums, faster/better results; self bleaching at home without supervision = risk of too long left on teeth, frosting, harmful ingredients.

Aesthetic complications: irregular results/stains, pale (unnatural white/blue), no effect on fillings/krones/facings (colour difference occurs), temporary white gums.

Temporaryity and vicious circle: results persist for several months to one year; risk for cycle of bleaching > sensitivity > discoloration > re-whitening that weakens teeth.

Bleaching methods: live teeth . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . Dead teeth, internal bleaching from the inside by dentist.

Costs: cosmetic dental care, not reimbursed by basic insurance, some supplementary insurances offer partial compensation.

Conclusion: personal balance between benefits (bright smile, self-confidence) and disadvantages (sensitivity, risk of irritation, unpredictable results, cost, repetition required) professional guidance significantly reduces risks.

FAQ: Is bleaching permanent? (no, 6 months to 2 years depending on lifestyle) . (more expensive, slightly more likely to be sensitive by heat, no panacea action comes from the gel) What to do in case of sensitivity? (toothpaste for sensitive teeth, avoid extreme temperatures 48 hours, fluoride gel/mouthwash;) Why is gum white after bleaching? (temporary dehydration/light irritation, usually harmless and disappears within hours; in persistent pain it may be a chemical burn) is bleaching bad for glaze? (in case of correct professional execution minimum/temporary damage, remineralizes glaze; frequent/incorrect bleaching may permanently weaken).
